m1 - MEASURED, NOT CLAIMING THE BEAD. THE DEFECT IS LIVE ON OUR REFERENCE FIXTURE RIGHT NOW, and it became live today as a direct consequence of a correct fix.

MEASURED on the worked example, 46 cells, THREE distinct present-term sets:

  20 cells   (no terms at all - external states, which use externalCost and never reach blend)
  13 cells   Semantic, Propositional, Entity, Granularity, Distortion            present-weight 3.200
  13 cells   Semantic, Propositional, Entity, Granularity, Distortion, Sensory   present-weight 3.350

  26 of 46 cells carry a recorded missing term.

SO THIRTEEN CELLS ARE COMPARED AGAINST THIRTEEN OTHERS ACROSS A 0.15 DIFFERENCE IN WHAT WAS EVEN MEASURABLE. Not hypothetically - that is the current posterior.

AND HERE IS THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR SCHEDULING. I checked whether this predates ee258bf. IT DOES NOT.

  BEFORE ee258bf: `val optional = Vector(CostTerm.Chart -> dChart, CostTerm.Structural -> dWl)`.
  Only two optional terms, and BOTH ARE ABSENT ON THIS FIXTURE (no charts). Sensory sat in `always`
  as a plain Double. So every blended cell had the identical six present terms. UNIFORM. The
  incommensurability was LATENT - real in the code, invisible in the data.

  AFTER ee258bf: Sensory moved to `optional`, 13 cells lost it, and the population split.

THIS IS NOT A CRITICISM OF ee258bf. That fix is correct and I argued for it. But its consequence is that a latent architectural defect became a live one, on our only substantial fixture, today. A term that can genuinely be absent is exactly what a bare sum over present terms cannot handle, so the moment we started recording absence honestly, the blend stopped being able to compare its own outputs.

WHICH ALSO EXPLAINS THE d_ent RESULT retrospectively: d_ent would have added a THIRD population at present-weight 2.800, and the 0.2 discount I measured is just this defect seen from one term's point of view.

I AM NOT CLAIMING THIS BEAD. It restructures the cost model and affects every alignment decision, and the chief has been managing my load deliberately today. But it now blocks two of my beads (bd-01M16M5ETH0QHFZ62KXZJ54PN9 and, through it, the traceability item C), and I have built four support carriers already - MassRatio, StepMass, SupportedScalar, ExternalMassReport - so if nobody else wants it I am the obvious hands.

Offering, not taking. The measurement above is the part that was missing either way.
